overview: The council received a briefing on the history and activities of the Energy and Environment Committee and reviewed updates on various city-led sustainability initiatives, including the Electrify Medford campaign and planned stormwater infrastructure improvements.

items.title: Approval of Minutes
items.summary: The council approved the minutes of the previous meeting.

items.title: Energy and Environment Committee Briefing
items.summary: Robert Paine presented the history and mission of the Medford Energy and Environment Committee, highlighting past initiatives like the McGlynn School wind turbine, the Harvest Your Energy Festival, and ongoing work on a tree ordinance.

items.title: Electrify Medford Campaign Update
items.summary: Brenda Pike announced the city was awarded a MassCEC Empower grant and provided updates on hiring energy coaches, adding a translation widget to the Go Green Medford website, and new free heat pump consultations through Mass Save.

items.title: Curbside Composting Program
items.summary: The city announced a free curbside composting program starting July 1 for residents in buildings with four units or less.

items.title: South Medford Stormwater Improvements
items.summary: The council discussed a grant application for construction of drainage improvements in South Medford and agreed to draft a letter of support for the project.

items.title: Transportation: Blue Bikes and Wellington Underpass
items.summary: The council reviewed the expansion of Blue Bike stations, including income-eligible membership options, and updates on the design of a pedestrian and cyclist underpass at the Wellington intersection.

items.title: MBTA Reduced Fares and Public Assistance
items.summary: Brenda Pike detailed eligibility for reduced MBTA fares and addressed delays in processing LIHEAP fuel assistance applications.
